correctness.rationale: Full explicit proof: finite-degree polynomial CRT gives convergence of low-prime geometric valuations; expected remainder of logarithms \(O(q^{-D}/(D+1))\) uniformly in degree; Sperner antichain bound with independent fair-Bernoulli factorization yields no atoms; Chernoff bound \(K_D=O(\log D)\) and degree–multiplicity profiles imply \(\exp(O((\log D)^2))\) intervals of radius \(q^{-D/2}\), hence Hausdorff dimension zero. Euler local factors yield exact moments. Exact rational verification of \(q=2\) through degree eight and \(q=3\) through degree five reproduced independently of closed moments.

value.rationale: The normalized reciprocal divisor sum is a canonical function-field analogue of the abundancy index and is motivated by current study of polynomial divisor statistics. Proving that its limit is both atomless and carried by a zero-dimensional set distinguishes three mutually exclusive probability types and explains the arithmetic source of thinness via degree histograms. The classification applies to every fixed prime power and gives exact moments; it is not an arbitrary slice, textbook restatement, or finite table recomputation.
